law: The workbench feature matrix is generated from the DX0 canonical exposure descriptors plus producer-registered capabilities. It replaces the manually curated compiler-demo tab list as the feature-coverage authority for the playground product; a literal hand-written feature list in workbench UI code is a coverage defect once PG2's generated explorer is the active authority.

vocabulary.dxOperationId: DX0 feature-exposure-contract.v1.json operation ids only; PG0 mints no parallel operation namespace. Each operationCoverage row must equal the joined DX0 row on hostExecutionClass, answerRail, browserExecutable and playground status, must carry the joined promotionBlocked state (absent means not blocked), and must carry the joined exposure.replayCase, the joined playground.blockedUntil route and replay case while blocked, and the joined playground.unlabelledAnalysisMerge pin (with its comparisonRailSelection) wherever DX0 records one; a row over a live unlabelled merge stays promotion-blocked and its routeObligation states the labelled-split/comparisonRail route, never a single TS-worker authority over the merge.
vocabulary.workbenchState: DX0 playgroundStatus enum (exposed, partial, missing) joined verbatim from the DX0 row; PG0 never restates it independently.
vocabulary.familyStateSource: exposed: every joined DX0 operation has workbenchState exposed; partial: at least one joined operation is exposed or partial, or a preserved PG0.1 surface ships while another part of the family is uncovered; missing: every joined operation has a shipping producer but no workbench route (the family renders as blocked/pending promotion, never as success); future: no shipping producer exists anywhere yet, so the family is a registered obligation with a named producing node and renders as the distinct future state, never as successful empty output.
vocabulary.answerRail: DX0 rails-policy.v1.json rails (semantic, inspection, comparison, none); inspection-rail answers stay labelled and never substitute semantic-rail answers.
vocabulary.hostExecutionClassSource: DX0 host-execution-class.v1.json; synonymous restatements describe but never define classes
vocabulary.completenessStateSource: DX0 product-receipt-basis.v1.json completenessStates; complete-empty is a successful empty answer and every other non-complete state is distinct from it

preservedSurface.obligation: Multifile editing, Vue/Svelte outputs, preview, timings, version selection, themes and compiler options keep working on every workbench cutover; a cutover that removes one of these before its surviving route exists is a regression, not a migration.

displacedRoute.description: Two hand-written output navs are displaced at the cutover: the allTabs list in packages/playground/src/output/Output.vue (preview, files, analysis, lint, outline, cssMatch, map, diagnostics, templateAst, cssVarFlow, depGraph, plus the ssr insert), a manually curated compiler-demo feature list, and the sibling Output|Why? nav in packages/playground/src/App.vue whose always-rendered Why? control mounts AuditTree.vue. displacedRoute.tabs maps every live tab mode to its owning feature family and panel, and displacedRoute.appNav maps every live App.vue nav control, so no user-visible surface loses its surviving producer at the cutover.
displacedRoute.cutoverRule: Characterize the existing user-visible surfaces first (displacedRoute.tabs binds each tab mode and displacedRoute.appNav binds each App.vue nav control to its owning family and panel), route each through its surviving producer (this matrix's featureFamilies rows), verify consumers, then remove the literal lists. The harness fails when an Output.vue tab mode or an App.vue nav control lacks a family-owned panel. Inert generated-matrix adapters may land before PG2 activates; after activation no two active feature-coverage authorities may coexist.
displacedRoute.deletionPopulationThisNode: empty: PG0 is contract-only and deletes nothing; the cutover executes in PG2 with this matrix as the generated obligation source.

appNav.description: packages/playground/src/App.vue renders a sibling output nav above the workbench output surface. The Output control hosts the Output.vue tab strip, whose live modes are owned one-for-one by displacedRoute.tabs; the Why? control mounts AuditTree.vue, the provenance-chain view over the component-meta audit pipeline (ProvenanceChain from getComponentMetaWithAudit whyLoaded/whyInstantiated; provenanceChain is null until the playground wires the WASM session, so the control currently renders AuditTree.vue's enable-footprint empty state).

featureFamilies.descriptorGap: DX0 registers no why/audit operation id; the App.vue Why? control (displacedRoute.appNav) mounts AuditTree.vue, the view over the component-meta provenance chain (ProvenanceChain from getComponentMetaWithAudit whyLoaded/whyInstantiated), and renders the enable-footprint empty state while the chain is unwired. The metadata family cannot hold it: DX0's lsp.component-meta gap evidence does not cite AuditTree.vue or App.vue, so this preserved live surface rides a descriptor-gap family; PG3's semantic and TypeInfo explorer registers the why/audit operation through DX1 as it exposes it

DX0 registers no runtime/SSR/HMR operation descriptor yet; PG9 isolated preview, PG10 SSR inspection, PG11 bundler/HMR and PG11D DOM/style probes register their operations through DX1 as they expose them

featureFamilies.futureProducer: PG14 interactive performance and invalidation laboratory; AC-RESOURCE equal-work corpus and real-client cost accounting bind there, and no general performance claim follows from a compiler microbenchmark; the family renders as the distinct future state, never as successful empty output

rules: PG0-AC1: a supported feature promoted by its producer (DX0 playground.status exposed, or promotionBlocked lifted) without a matching executable workbench matrix row fails coverage; the matrix is the coverage authority, and pg0.test.mjs joins every DX0 operation id to exactly one operationCoverage row with equality on class, rail, browserExecutable, status and promotionBlocked, plus the joined replayCase, blockedUntil route/replay case and the unlabelledAnalysisMerge pin where DX0 records one.

PG0-AC2: a capability with no shipping producer is future: its family row carries familyState future with a named futureProducer, its results render as the distinct future/unsupported completeness state, and it is never presented as successful empty output (complete-empty).
PG0-AC3: every supported feature has a runnable route, a source-linked result or explanation, and a replay scenario; a route that cannot be replayed is not executable coverage.

A NativeOnly operation's workbench route is explicitly selected native execution through the DX4/DX5 companion (or the BWH1-admitted browser semantic host where its build proves the closure); an inactive card, a hidden substitution engine or an unlabelled Portable stand-in are each coverage failures, not partial coverage.

PG0-AC-EXPOSURE: every operation this train exposes supplies its DX1 registration, executable playground adapter and replay case; until the DX1 explorer exists the schema and case are registered in this matrix (each operationCoverage row carries its joined DX0 exposure.replayCase and, while blocked, the blockedUntil replay case) and product promotion stays blocked on executable exposure.

PG0.4: a newly registered framework or profile acquires these obligations automatically when its descriptors register; the workbench does not implement missing framework compilers and does not replace TypeScript.
Inspection-rail results stay labelled with their own provenance and never substitute semantic-rail answers; generated coordinates are never presented as authored coordinates.

Every matrix result binds the DX0 product-receipt-basis field set, and stale-basis results (old source, old project, old engine, old worker, wrong result handle) are rejected rather than published as current.
